standard_position: All four standard exceptions must be included: (i) publicly available information; (ii) already in recipient's possession; (iii) received from a third party without restriction; (iv) independently developed without use of confidential information
fallback_positions: Accept three of four exceptions if the missing one poses low practical risk given the specific engagement
Accept modified language (e.g., requiring written evidence of prior possession) provided all four categories are conceptually covered
red_line: Never accept an NDA with fewer than three standard exceptions. The "independently developed" exception is critical for diversified organizations
decision_logic: Standard exceptions protect the receiving party from being held liable for information it already knew, independently developed, or received from other legitimate sources. Without these exceptions, a large, diversified organization could inadvertently breach the NDA simply by using knowledge it already possessed. Some NDAs omit one or more standard exceptions — particularly the "independently developed" exception. For large organizations with multiple business units conducting parallel R&D, this omission creates significant risk.
escalation_logic: If the "independently developed" exception is missing and cannot be added, escalate.
